Marissa / Nikhil,

Thanks again for the call this morning — that was super helpful. I wanted to capture the high-level pain and goals on our side and ask for a short recap of what Redwood recommends for Dedicated capacity.

Key pain points we discussed:
- Latency spikes affecting our realtime triage UI (p95 sometimes > 800ms under load)
- Cost unpredictability with current bursty traffic patterns and inference caching gaps
- Data isolation / PHI handling requirements for certain customer classes

Goals / success criteria:
- Stable p95 latency under 200ms for the 90th percentile of queries in production
- Predictable monthly spend with committed capacity and clear overage billing
- Network-level isolation (VPC peering / private endpoints) + audit logs for compliance

Can you send a short dedicated-capacity recap (GPU types, initial sizing, scaling plan, SLA targets, and any on-prem/VPC options)? Also loop in procurement if you have a standard procurement path/contract.

Thanks,
Samira

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear summary. Below is a concise Dedicated Capacity recommendation based on what you shared. I also attached a 1-page PDF and a mutual action plan workbook for procurement/technical owners.

Attachment stubs:
- dedicated-capacity-summary.pdf (PDF, 412 KB)
- mutual-action-plan.xlsx (Excel, 98 KB)

Redwood Dedicated — proposed plan (high level):
1) Reserved capacity profile:
   - Initial commit: 2x NVIDIA A100 (40GB) instances, colocated in us-west-2
   - Burst capacity: auto-burst to up to 8x A100s using reserved pool + burst credits
   - Option to upgrade to H100s for large-context models (add-on during next quarter)

2) Isolation & compliance:
   - VPC peering and private egress; private endpoints for inference traffic
   - Customer-managed keys (KMS) + audit logs exported to your logging account
   - SOC 2 artifacts available; we can provide a redacted report and control mappings for PHI handling

3) Scaling & routing policy:
   - Steady-state handled by reserved pool (2x A100) for baseline throughput
   - Autoscale policy: add 2 GPUs per minute up to max burst (8 GPUs) based on queue depth and p95 latency signals
   - Smart routing: route non-critical/long-running batches to lower-cost pool or quantized model variants to protect latency SLOs

4) SLA & SLO targets:
   - Availability SLA (Dedicated): 99.9% monthly uptime for the serving runtime
   - Latency targets: p50 < 50ms, p95 < 200ms for 512-token requests under steady-state reserved capacity
   - We provide latency and cost dashboards per model/route and token-level cost breakdowns

5) Cost / billing model:
   - Monthly committed capacity fee (covers reserved pool + baseline support) + usage-based token billing for overage
   - Clear overage pricing tiers in the mutual action plan (attached)

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll share a short SOW / pricing summary for procurement (include Ben Howell on procurement) — target by EOD Thu 3/5
- Technical deep-dive with Soojin to validate model footprint and exact GPU sizing (schedule 60 min next week)
- Trial window: 30-day pilot on the proposed reserved pool with monitoring and weekly checkpoints

If that aligns, I’ll loop in our finance/procurement contacts and send the draft SOW.

Best,
Marissa Cole

1) On-prem / private deployment: is there a staged option where we start with Dedicated (Redwood-managed in our VPC) and then move to on-prem if needed for certain PHI workloads? Any timeline/cost ballpark?
2) Data residency: we need to ensure data for EU patients stays in EU regions — is regional isolation a simple toggle or requires separate reserved pools?
3) Pilot billing: can the 30-day pilot be structured as a temporary committed pool (credit against first month) so procurement can approve more easily?

Also, can Soojin include a short model-sizing checklist so we can prep model artifacts before the technical deep-dive?

Hi Samira / Ben — looping Ben into the plan and answering the clarifying questions below.

1) Staged path to on-prem: yes — we offer a staged migration. Start with Redwood Dedicated in your VPC (managed control plane) and then transition to on-prem (air-gapped package) when you’re ready. Typical timeline: 8–12 weeks for on-prem packaging + onboarding; pricing is provided as an enterprise add-on (I’ll include ballpark numbers in the SOW).

2) Regional isolation: we can provision separate reserved pools per region. For EU patient data, we recommend a dedicated EU pool (e.g., eu-west-1) with region-restricted routing policies.

3) Pilot billing: we can structure the 30-day pilot as a temporary committed pool and credit it against the first month to simplify procurement approvals. I’ll capture this in the mutual action plan and SOW.

Soojin will send a short model-sizing checklist (artifact list + typical memory/latency expectations) within the next business day.
